routes.label: Calculate each rider’s time by leg

question: Minnie rides on a flat road at \(20\) kilometers per hour (kph), downhill at \(30\) kph, and uphill at \(5\) kph. Penny rides on a flat road at \(30\) kph, downhill at \(40\) kph, and uphill at \(10\) kph. Minnie goes from town \(A\) to town \(B,\) a distance of \(10\) km all uphill, then from town \(B\) to town \(C,\) a distance of \(15\) km all downhill, and then back to town \(A,\) a distance of \(20\) km on the flat. Penny goes the other way around using the same route. How many more minutes does it take Minnie to complete the \(45\)-km ride than it takes Penny?
solution:
Reversing the route turns each uphill segment into a downhill segment and each downhill segment into an uphill segment. For each leg, use time equals distance divided by speed.

Minnie rides \(10\) km uphill, \(15\) km downhill, and \(20\) km on flat road. Her total time in hours is
\[
T_M=\frac{10}{5}+\frac{15}{30}+\frac{20}{20}
=2+\frac12+1
=\frac72.
\]
Penny follows \(A\) to \(C\) to \(B\) to \(A\). She rides \(20\) km on flat road, \(15\) km uphill, and \(10\) km downhill. Her total time in hours is
\[
T_P=\frac{20}{30}+\frac{15}{10}+\frac{10}{40}
=\frac23+\frac32+\frac14
=\frac{8+18+3}{12}
=\frac{29}{12}.
\]
The difference is
\[
T_M-T_P=\frac{42}{12}-\frac{29}{12}=\frac{13}{12}\text{ hours}.
\]
Since each hour has \(60\) minutes, Minnie takes
\[
\frac{13}{12}\cdot60=65
\]
more minutes. The answer is \(65\), choice **C**.
